title: 3Sum
summary: Find every distinct triple of values that adds to zero.

contractDetails.constraints: The array has 3–3,000 integers in [−100,000, 100,000]. A value can appear multiple times in one triple only when that many positions contain it.
contractDetails.output-checking: Compare the set of sorted triples and reject duplicate triples.

statement: Find every distinct triple of values that adds to zero. Each triple must use three different positions. Return each value combination once, in any order, with any ordering within each triple.

examples.explanation: There are two ways to pair values with −6.
Multiple choices of positions give the same value triple.
Three negative numbers cannot sum to zero.

constraints: The array has 3–3,000 integers in [−100,000, 100,000]. A value can appear multiple times in one triple only when that many positions contain it.
hints: Conceptual: A choice for the first number leaves a two-number target.
Directional: Sort the values so you can look for the remaining pair from opposite ends.
Implementation: Fix one value, scan the suffix with two pointers, and skip equal adjacent values for the anchor and after a match.
complexityAnalysis: O(n²) time and O(n) auxiliary space when sorting a copy, excluding returned triples. Each distinct anchor can trigger one linear scan.
